items.title: Functoriality of the equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on a scheme and on its big and small sites
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes f : T to S the proposition has three parts: the equivalences of categories identifying quasi-coherent modules on S with those on the big and small sites are compatible with pullback, in the sense that pulling back the sheaf associated to a quasi-coherent module is the sheaf associated to the pulled back module; the corresponding compatibility with pushforward fails, and not even the statement can be made precise in general; and when f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and the topology is Zariski or etale, pushforward of quasi-coherent modules along f and along the induced morphism of small sites stays quasi-coherent and the square comparing pushforward with the association F to F^a commutes (statement lines 3108-3135). The claim is H3 for two reasons. First, part (2) is carried by an explicit counterexample, the quasi-compact open immersion of the punctured plane into the plane, where the pushforward of the structure sheaf of the punctured plane is the structure sheaf of the plane but becomes zero after base change to the origin; the author also explains why no precise statement is available, namely that compatibility over the big sites would force pushforward to commute with arbitrary base change (proof lines 3140-3150). Second, part (3) is a separate argument that turns the asserted equality of sheaves into a statement about sections over an etale morphism into S and identifies the two sides by flat base change (proof lines 3153-3161). What keeps this below a routine derivation is precisely that a counterexample has to be exhibited for one part and a flat base change identification carried out for another.
